main_text.p: mittitur, semper justum esse censebitur. Nec quod fit legel.48 §.in permittente, tutum quem reddit in conscientia, etiamsi sit extra legis poenam.contrarium. D. Unde quaesitum, utrum judici liceat reos condemnatos cogere, ut singulari certamine contendentes invicem conficiant? Respondeo quod non, neque enim in judicis arbitrio situm est nocentem quomodocunque libuerit, punire.Acquir. domin. Anton. Quaest. Consil. 61.n.5. & 6. Et quia reus condemnatus, tantum tenetur poenam quam meretur ejus delictum perferre ac pati, ut justitiae vindicativae fiat satis; non vero alium quem affligere.Grot. de jur. belli & Pac.l. 2,c 1. num. 14. Et quia afflicto non est superaddenda afflictio; quae tum superadditur, cum vel invitus ad aliquid agendum cogitur, ut tamen non ipse, sed alius laedatur; vel forte duriori mortis genere, quàm fuisset perituru-rus, si per carnificis funestam

page.notes: Running head "De" is partly damaged; read as "De" [?]. Page number "81" is partly worn; read as 81 [?]. Catchword "ma" is cut off at the edge; read as "ma[?]". Marginal citation "Pac.l." is hard to read; the abbreviation may be "Pae.l." or "Pac.l." Citation "6i.n.5." may be "61.n.5." Several small margin notes are blurred and partly split across lines (e.g. "contra-rium", "Quaest."), so their exact letters are uncertain. The hyphenated "peritu-rus" and "Re-spondeo" are kept as printed. The line "affligé-re" is read as "affligere" with its break at the hyphen.
